items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-16
items.q: That's P. Ron, Robichaud, and this fellow played a cornerhead of brass band, Manuel Perez. Now they played conventional music.

ctx.x: You don't see anything in front of me that I take notes from, only just from what comes to my mind. That's why I don't have it in chronological order. I can only tell you what I can think of at the time. Maybe my talk may be gobbled up a little bit, that I might put this one before the other one, the other one before the other one. But I am telling you the true facts of this music. It was in Chicago where I changed the rhythm. They had a certain dance team. They were doing a castle walk. And up in the north,…
Can you hold it a second?

items.q: I'm not aware of the fact that you all are the starters of Sister Kate up north... assure you that you will receive all assistance that I can give along the lines of placing this and all of the numbers that I have and that you may be able to use... ctx.x: Well you mentioned Pierron's band and what type of music they play. I forgot to mention it was in the year about 1915. I think Pierron then used mostly string instruments. And he played regular conventional ragtime like I had right on records that was of that date of error. There's some things I'd like to tell you that I may have forgotten to mention. We played for two silent movies. One of them is in the Good For Nothing by Carlisle Blackwell. He was the leading man. And her shot was Charlie Chapman. This would…

This is a letter. It says, It says, From A.J. P. Ron, 1734 Annette Street, New Orleans, Louisiana. The dateline is August 13, 1922. Mr. D. My dear Mr. LaRocca, yours of the fifth INST comp was received and very sorry indeed for the delay and great suspense that you no doubt suffered. items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: I had never known P. Ron but I heard him play.

ctx.x: Now what did people object to in the dance?

Well they said we had a sexual music that we were ruining the morals of the girls. They, people would get out there and they'd forget they were dancing, standing in one spot and starting moving around. In other words the great masters tried to move them. But they didn't succeed. I guess ours was like wine or good wine. When the people would get interested in our music. They'd stand there. Some of them would dance around. Stand there and they just moved themselves like worms. And many of the times we'd sneak off…

many of the places we had returning engagements. Through my files, you'll be able to see the office of jobs we had. And all the New Orleans boys was not working. And if I'd have had a thousand men that could play our music, I could have been a millionaire today because I had jobs for all of them. But there was none of them could fit the bill. In this one-night stands, we came back. And it was a tough job, riding all night to go to another place. For instance, you'd jump from Philadelphia to Pittsburgh. It was…
